questions.q: What type of tissue is the epidermis, and is it vascular?
options: Simple cuboidal epithelium with many capillaries
Stratified squamous keratinised epithelium with no blood vessels
questions.explain: It is nourished by diffusion from dermal capillaries.

open.q: What type of tissue is the epidermis, and is it vascular?

questions.q: Name the strata of the epidermis from deep to superficial.
questions.explain: Cells migrate upwards from the basal layer, keratinise and are shed.

open.q: Name the strata of the epidermis from deep to superficial.

questions.q: Which epidermal layer is present only in thick skin (palms and soles)?
questions.explain: It is a thin, clear layer between the granulosum and the corneum.

open.q: Which epidermal layer is present only in thick skin (palms and soles)?

questions.q: Which epidermal layer contains actively dividing cells?
questions.explain: Also called the stratum germinativum.

open.q: Which epidermal layer contains actively dividing cells?

questions.q: In which epidermal layer are melanocytes mainly found?
questions.explain: They are derived from the neural crest and transfer melanin to keratinocytes.

open.q: In which epidermal layer are melanocytes mainly found?

questions.q: What is the function of Langerhans cells?
questions.explain: They capture antigens in the epidermis and carry them to lymph nodes.

open.q: What is the function of Langerhans cells?

questions.q: What is the function of Merkel cells?
options: They act as touch receptors in the basal epidermis
questions.explain: They are associated with sensory nerve endings.

open.q: What is the function of Merkel cells?

questions.q: What is the superficial layer of the dermis called?
questions.explain: It forms dermal papillae that interlock with the epidermis. The deeper reticular layer is dense irregular connective tissue.

open.q: What is the superficial layer of the dermis called?

questions.q: Which vitamin is synthesised in the skin on exposure to sunlight?
questions.explain: UVB converts 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholecalciferol in the epidermis.

open.q: Which vitamin is synthesised in the skin on exposure to sunlight?

questions.q: Which precursor in the skin is converted to cholecalciferol by UV light?
questions.explain: Cholecalciferol is then hydroxylated in the liver and kidney.

open.q: Which precursor in the skin is converted to cholecalciferol by UV light?

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a function of the skin?
questions.explain: Insulin is made by the pancreas.

questions.q: Which nerve fibres supply eccrine sweat glands?
questions.explain: This is an exception: sympathetic postganglionic fibres that release acetylcholine.

open.q: Which nerve fibres supply eccrine sweat glands?

questions.q: Where are apocrine sweat glands mainly found?
questions.explain: They become active at puberty. Bacterial breakdown of their secretion causes body odour.

open.q: Where are apocrine sweat glands mainly found?

questions.q: By what mechanism do sebaceous glands release their secretion?
questions.explain: The whole cell breaks down and is released as sebum.

open.q: By what mechanism do sebaceous glands release their secretion?

questions.q: Which skin areas have no sebaceous glands?
questions.explain: Most sebaceous glands open into hair follicles.

open.q: Which skin areas have no sebaceous glands?

questions.q: Compared with plasma, is sweat hypotonic, isotonic or hypertonic?
questions.explain: Primary sweat is isotonic, but NaCl is reabsorbed in the duct.

open.q: Compared with plasma, is sweat hypotonic, isotonic or hypertonic?

questions.q: What is raised in sweat in cystic fibrosis?
questions.explain: Defective CFTR stops chloride reabsorption in the sweat duct, which is the basis of the sweat test.

open.q: What is raised in sweat in cystic fibrosis?

questions.q: Sebum production is stimulated by which hormones?
questions.explain: This is why acne begins at puberty.

open.q: Sebum production is stimulated by which hormones?

questions.q: How does the number of melanocytes compare between dark-skinned and light-skinned people?
options: Dark skin has many more melanocytes than light skin
About the same; dark skin's melanocytes are more active
Melanocytes are completely absent in light skin
Light skin has more melanocytes than dark skin
questions.explain: Colour depends on the amount and type of melanin produced and its distribution, not on the number of melanocytes. Activity is higher in people from the tropics.

open.q: How does the number of melanocytes compare between dark-skinned and light-skinned people?

questions.q: Which gland is the most numerous sweat gland in the human body?
questions.explain: Eccrine sweat glands are the most numerous, found over almost the entire body surface.

open.q: Which type of sweat gland is most numerous in the human body?

questions.q: What is the main function of sebum?
questions.explain: Sebum oils the skin and hair, reducing water loss and providing some antibacterial protection.

open.q: What is the main function of sebum?

questions.q: Which stimulus primarily controls sebaceous gland secretion?
questions.explain: Sebaceous glands are stimulated mainly by androgens, which is why acne often appears at puberty.

open.q: Which hormone group primarily stimulates sebaceous gland secretion?

questions.q: Where do eccrine sweat glands open on the skin surface?
options: Onto the skin surface via a duct
questions.explain: Eccrine glands open directly onto the skin surface through a sweat pore, not into hair follicles.

open.q: Do eccrine sweat glands open into hair follicles or directly onto the skin surface?

questions.q: Which component of eccrine sweat is primarily responsible for its antibacterial action?
questions.explain: Lactic acid lowers skin pH and lysozyme breaks bacterial cell walls, giving sweat antibacterial properties.

open.q: Which two components give eccrine sweat its antibacterial properties?

questions.q: Apocrine sweat glands become functionally active at which stage of life?
questions.explain: Apocrine glands are inactive until puberty, when androgens trigger their development.

open.q: At what stage of life do apocrine sweat glands become active?

questions.q: Which gland is responsible for the odour of the axilla after bacterial breakdown of its secretion?
questions.explain: Apocrine secretions are rich in organic compounds that bacteria break down to produce body odour.

open.q: Which gland's secretion produces body odour after bacterial breakdown?

questions.q: What is the main cell type of the epidermis?
questions.explain: Keratinocytes make up about 90% of epidermal cells and produce keratin.

open.q: What is the most abundant cell type in the epidermis?

questions.q: Which epidermal cell type produces melanin?
questions.explain: Melanocytes in the stratum basale synthesize melanin and transfer it to keratinocytes.

open.q: Which epidermal cell produces melanin?

questions.q: What is the role of melanin in the skin?
questions.explain: Melanin absorbs UV light and protects nuclear DNA from damage.

open.q: What is the main protective role of melanin in skin?

questions.q: Which skin function is mainly carried out by the dermis rather than the epidermis?
questions.explain: The dermis is rich in collagen and elastin fibres that give skin its strength and elasticity.

open.q: Which skin layer provides most of its tensile strength and elasticity?

questions.q: What is the main tissue of the hypodermis?
questions.explain: The hypodermis is mainly adipose tissue and loose connective tissue, providing insulation and cushioning.

open.q: What is the main tissue of the hypodermis?

questions.q: Which skin function is impaired when the epidermis is extensively damaged by burns?
options: Barrier against water loss and infection
questions.explain: Loss of epidermis removes the waterproof barrier, causing fluid loss and risk of infection.

open.q: Which barrier function is lost when the epidermis is extensively burned?

questions.q: Which sensation is detected by Meissner corpuscles in the dermal papillae?
questions.explain: Meissner corpuscles are rapidly adapting receptors for light touch, especially in fingertips.

open.q: Which type of sensation is detected by Meissner corpuscles?

questions.q: Which receptor is responsible for detecting deep pressure and vibration?
questions.explain: Pacinian corpuscles are deep dermal receptors that detect high-frequency vibration and deep pressure.

open.q: Which skin receptor detects deep pressure and vibration?

questions.q: What gives the skin its waterproof property?
questions.explain: Lipids secreted into the intercellular spaces of the stratum corneum make the skin waterproof.

open.q: What makes the skin waterproof?

questions.q: A patient has a burn that destroys the entire epidermis and part of the dermis. Which skin function is immediately lost?
options: Barrier against infection and fluid loss
questions.explain: Destruction of the epidermis removes the main physical barrier, leading to infection and fluid loss.

open.q: Which function is immediately lost when the epidermis is destroyed by a burn?

questions.q: Which gland is a modified apocrine sweat gland that secretes cerumen?
questions.explain: Ceruminous glands in the external auditory canal are modified apocrine glands that produce earwax.

open.q: Which gland secretes cerumen in the external auditory canal?

questions.q: Which gland produces the watery secretion responsible for thermoregulation through evaporative cooling?
questions.explain: Eccrine sweat is watery and evaporates to cool the body surface.

open.q: Which gland produces watery sweat for evaporative cooling?

questions.q: Which skin layer contains the blood vessels that provide oxygen and nutrients to the epidermis?
questions.explain: The dermis is vascular and nourishes the avascular epidermis by diffusion.

open.q: Which skin layer contains the blood vessels that nourish the epidermis?

questions.q: Where are eccrine sweat glands located within the skin?
options: Deep in the dermis or hypodermis
questions.explain: Eccrine glands are coiled tubular glands located deep in the dermis or upper hypodermis, with ducts opening onto the surface.

open.q: In which skin layer are eccrine sweat glands mainly located?

questions.q: What is the role of the dermal papillae?
options: Increasing surface area between epidermis and dermis
questions.explain: Dermal papillae interlock with the epidermis, increasing the surface area for exchange and strengthening the bond.

open.q: What is the function of dermal papillae?

questions.q: Which vitamin is produced when 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin is exposed to UV light?
questions.explain: UVB converts 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) in the epidermis.

open.q: Which vitamin is produced in the skin after UV exposure of 7-dehydrocholesterol?

questions.q: Which component of sweat is primarily responsible for the salty taste?
questions.explain: Sodium chloride is the main salt in eccrine sweat and gives it a salty taste.

open.q: Which salt is the main reason sweat tastes salty?

questions.q: Which layer of the epidermis is composed of dead, flattened, keratin-filled cells?
questions.explain: The stratum corneum consists of dead, anucleate keratin-filled squames that form the skin's surface barrier.

open.q: Which epidermal layer consists of dead, keratin-filled cells?

questions.q: What is the main function of keratin in the epidermis?
questions.explain: Keratin is a tough fibrous protein that gives skin its mechanical strength and water resistance.

open.q: What is the main function of keratin in the epidermis?

questions.q: A patient with extensive burns loses the ability to sweat over the burned area. Which function has been lost?
questions.explain: Loss of eccrine sweat glands prevents evaporative cooling, impairing thermoregulation.

open.q: Which function is lost when burns destroy the sweat glands over an area of skin?

questions.q: Which type of gland is found in the external auditory canal and helps protect the ear from infection?
questions.explain: Ceruminous glands secrete cerumen, which traps dust and has antibacterial properties.

open.q: Which gland in the ear canal secretes protective earwax?

questions.q: Which skin layer contains hair follicles and sebaceous glands?
questions.explain: Hair follicles and sebaceous glands are located in the dermis and often extend into the hypodermis.

open.q: In which skin layer are hair follicles and sebaceous glands found?

questions.q: Which function of skin is most directly served by its rich sensory nerve supply?
questions.explain: Skin sensory receptors detect touch, pressure, pain and temperature, providing protective information.

open.q: Which function is served by the skin's sensory nerve supply?
